Compare the runs and label every difference

Source: R/compare.R
compare_runs.Rd

Compares the baseline's and the candidate's runs step by step and gives each difference one mechanical kind. The labels say what differs, not whether it is intended: that judgement is left to the reader.

Usage

compare_runs(
  d,
  tol = 1e-04,
  min_time = 0.03,
  min_ratio = 1.2,
  min_timings = 5L,
  plot_tol = 0,
  api = TRUE,
  accept = NULL,
  keep_metadata = FALSE
)

Arguments

d

A dossier().

tol

Relative tolerance for numbers.

min_time, min_ratio

Timing rule: only steps whose median takes at least min_time seconds in one version are labelled, and only when the median ratio is at least min_ratio (or at most 1 / min_ratio). The default floor of 30 ms reflects the 10 ms resolution of the process timer on Windows.

min_timings

Fewest timings per version for a slower or faster label. The rule asks that all of one version's timings lie beyond the other's; with two timings a side that happens by chance one time in three, with five a side one time in 126, with six (the default reps = 3 in both runs of a version) one time in 462. Steps with fewer timings show their times without a label.

plot_tol

Largest share of differing pixels (0 to 1) at which two images of the same size still count as the same plot, for anti-aliasing or font noise. Needs the png package; without it plots are compared by checksum only.

api

Compare the exports and function signatures of the two versions.

accept

Rules for differences already read and accepted: a CSV file written by accept_differences() or a data frame with its columns. Accepted differences keep their rows, marked accepted, and are left out of the counts of print(), write_dossier_md() and check_differences().

keep_metadata

Keep differences in the package's own DESCRIPTION fields. By default, a value or element difference whose path ends in a field of the package's installed DESCRIPTION (Version, Packaged, Built, ...) and whose two sides are that field in the two versions is left out and counted: an example that prints sessionInfo() or packageDescription() shows them, and they differ between any two versions.

Value

An object of class pkgdossier_comparison, with methods for print(), summary(), differences(), write_dossier_html() and write_dossier_json(). Its $dossier is d, so the stages can be called again from the result: compare_runs(cmp$dossier, tol = 1e-3).

Details

KindRuleSeverity
unstablethe two runs of one version disagree; the step is not compared further0
error_newthe step errors only under the candidate1
field_removedan element path (x$a$b, x@slot, a data-frame column) only in the baseline1
condition_class_changedan error or warning with the same message but a different class2
value_moveda number whose relative change exceeds tol, a number that became or stopped being NA, or a short string that changed2
warning_newa warning message only the candidate gives2
output_changedthe console transcript or the printed value differs (one row per stream), unless every changed line differs only in printed numbers within tol3
plot_changedthe PNG files differ (checksum) or their number differs; with the png package, the share of differing pixels is reported, and images whose share is at most plot_tol are not labelled3
slower, fasterfor timed steps of min_time seconds or more with at least min_timings timings per version: the candidate's timings all lie above (below) the baseline's by more than 5 ms (half the Windows timer tick) and the median ratio is beyond min_ratio3
warning_gonea warning message only the baseline gives4
field_addedan element path only in the candidate4
error_fixedthe step errors only under the baseline4

With api = TRUE, the exports and function signatures of the two versions are compared too, without running anything; these differences are listed under the scenario (namespace), with the function as the step and the argument as the path:

KindRuleSeverity
export_removedan export of the baseline is gone (or is no longer a function)1
argument_removedan argument of an exported function is gone1
argument_new_requireda new argument without a default, or an argument that lost its default1
arguments_reorderedthe arguments both versions have come in a different order2
default_changedan argument's default differs2
argument_addeda new argument with a default4
export_addeda new export4

Coverage. The comparison also records which exported functions the scenarios use (directly or through the objects they produce), which they do not, and which candidate NEWS bullets no step or API difference was matched to: changes the dossier did not exercise. print(), the report and the Markdown summary show it.

A step that errors under both versions is a scenario problem rather than a finding: it is reported with status error_both and compared no further (apart from a change of the error's class), unless under only one version R stopped in it, it timed out or pkgdossier could not capture it, which is error_new (or error_fixed). A vignette chunk run with error = TRUE runs on after an error, as knitr runs it, and the errors it shows its readers are part of its console output (Error: ...), compared with the rest; an error from a package that is not installed stays an error. A step that errors under one version is compared no further. Numbers that differ by less than tol are counted, not listed: such differences come from optimisers and floating point, not from a change in method.

NEWS candidates. The candidate's NEWS (NEWS.md or a plain-text NEWS, at the top level or in inst/, or else inst/NEWS.Rd through the news database R builds when installing it) is read from the sections written after the baseline's version. For each step, the bullets that name a function of the package the step uses are attached to the step and to each of its differences (column news). A function is "used" when its name appears in the step's code, when it is a method for the class of the step's last visible value (so print.myclass() for a printed myclass object), or when it produced an object the step uses: fit <- fit_model(d) in one step makes summary(fit) in a later step use fit_model() too, following assignments through the scenario. A bullet "names" a function as fn(), pkg::fn(), `fn`, or, for names with a dot or an underscore, the bare name. A difference whose step has no such bullet gets no_news = TRUE. A large release can have dozens of bullets for a step, so each difference keeps at most three, those naming an element of its path first (converged for fit$diagnostics$converged), then those using a word that fits its kind (plot for plot_changed). This finds candidates only; whether a bullet covers the change is for the reader.

The comparison reads the stored runs and takes their order and repeats from them. It stops when a version was prepared again after its runs were made (its NEWS and provenance would no longer describe them), and warns when the dossier's run settings differ from those the runs were made with; run_scenarios() makes them again. Comparing is cheap: call it again with other tolerances, without running anything. Timings are shown but no step is labelled slower or faster when runs went at the same time, or when some runs were reused from an earlier call while others were made anew (after a fix, the baseline's runs are reused): ABBA's balance against drift in machine load holds only within one call. run_scenarios(d, force = TRUE) makes all runs together.

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- example_dossier()
prepare_versions(d, quiet = TRUE)
run_scenarios(d, quiet = TRUE)
cmp <- compare_runs(d)
cmp

#> 3 scenario(s), 28 step(s) compared, 2 not run; abba runs, 3 timed repeats per timed step
